quote: Rationale Lösung der quadratischen Ungleichung $\overset{2}{f}(x_1, \dots x_n) \lesseqgtr 0$ d.h. Abbildung des inneren eines Kegelschnittes, einer Fläche zweiter Ord auf eine{+r+} Ebene, den Raum etc...
english: Rational solution of the quadratic inequality f(x_1,...,x_n) ≤/≥ 0, i.e. mapping of the interior of a conic, of a second-order surface, onto a plane, onto space, etc.
topic: Notes on forms (binary, quadratic, ternary cubic) whose discriminant cases can be satisfied rationally, on the rational solution of quadratic inequalities as a mapping of regions, a remark on the nature of definitions, and the start of a note on an everywhere-convergent power series.

triage.modern_statement: Hilbert's note asks for a rational parametrization of the semialgebraic set cut out by one quadratic inequality. Given a real quadratic polynomial f(x_1,...,x_n), find a rational map from R^(n-1) (or R^n) whose image is exactly the region {f ≤ 0} or {f ≥ 0}. Examples are the interior of a conic or the inside of a quadric surface. Equivalently: is such a region a 'regular image' of Euclidean space, meaning the image of a rational map with no poles on the domain? This is a special case of the modern problem of characterizing which semialgebraic subsets of R^m are polynomial or regular images of some R^n.
triage.answered_by: The general framing was posed explicitly by J. M. Gamboa at the Oberwolfach 'Reelle algebraische Geometrie' week in June 1990. It was developed systematically by J. F. Fernando, J. M. Gamboa and C. Ueno, starting with 'Polynomial images of R^n' (J. Pure Appl. Algebra, 2003) and continuing through papers up to 2024–2025. The sources I found do not credit any of this to Hilbert's note. They also do not explicitly state that interiors of conics or quadrics are regular images; I am inferring that from the scope of this research program, not reading it in a source.

evidence.claim: In the 1990 Oberwolfach real algebraic geometry week, Gamboa proposed characterizing the semialgebraic subsets of R^m that are polynomial or regular images of some R^n.
Fernando, Gamboa and Ueno's survey describes the program: building explicit polynomial and regular maps onto large families of semialgebraic sets, and finding obstructions to being such images.

Fernando and Gamboa (2003) treat quadratic regions in the plane as basic test cases. For example, the exterior {u^2+v^2>1} of the closed unit disc is not a polynomial image of R^2, while the open quadrant is.
A related problem was posed by Gamboa in the 1990s at Oberwolfach; a 2008 note says deciding whether a set is the polynomial image of a Euclidean space 'has revealed as a difficult task'.
Recent work (2024–2025) studies polynomial and regular images of closed balls and spheres, so the research area is still active.

triage.why: The note is short but recognizable. It asks for rational maps from a plane or space whose image is exactly the region where a quadratic form is ≤ 0 or ≥ 0, such as the inside of a conic or quadric. For closed regions this is close to elementary; for example, z -> 2z/(1+|z|^2) maps the plane onto the closed unit disc (my own example, not from the sources). It is not among Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem, and I found no source that cites this note. The modern version is Gamboa's 1990 problem on polynomial and regular images of R^n. Fernando–Gamboa–Ueno have studied it extensively, using quadratic regions such as discs, disc exteriors and quadrants as basic examples, and it remains an active area. However, my searches ran out before I could find a source stating outright that the open disc or open ball is a regular image of R^n. So 'solved' for Hilbert's specific case is my inference, not a cited result, and confidence is low.
